lessons.title: Get ready! What you will learn

pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 📐 **Strand 3 — Geometry And Measurement**
Shape, space, measurement, position and movement — the mathematics of the world around us.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B8.3.2)
- B8.3.2.2 — Demonstrate understanding of the addition and subtraction of vectors and their applications in solving basic problems.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- add vectors graphically (nose-to-tail) and in component form
- subtract vectors and multiply a vector by a scalar
- find the magnitude of a resultant vector
- use the conditions for equal vectors to find unknowns

pages.title: Adding, subtracting and multiplying vectors
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Add, subtract and find the scalar multiplication of vectors in component form.
Curriculum indicator B8.3.2.2.1
## Graphical addition
To add vec{AB} and vec{BC}, place them **nose to tail**: the second vector starts where the first one ends. The **resultant** vec{AC} goes from the start of the first to the end of the second.
[[fig:m8-f43|Figure 11.1: AB + BC = AC]]
## ✏️ Example 11.1
Using the grid, find vec{AB} + vec{BC} when vec{AB} = col{3;1} and vec{BC} = col{1;3}.
**Solution**
Draw vec{AB} 3 right and 1 up; from B draw vec{BC} 1 right and 3 up. Read the resultant from A to C: vec{AC} **=** col{4;4}.
## Component form
> 🔑 **Key idea: Vector operations** — If vec{AB} = col{a;b} and vec{BC} = col{c;d} then: vec{AB} + vec{BC} = col{a + c;b + d}; vec{AB} − vec{BC} = col{a − c;b − d}; and for a scalar k: kcol{x;y} = col{kx;ky}.
## ✏️ Example 11.2
If p = col{−1;2}, q = col{4;3} and r = col{−2;5}, find: a) 3q − 2p b) r − 3p c) q − p + 2r
**Solution**
a) 3**q** = col{12;9}, 2**p** = col{−2;4}. 3**q** − 2**p** = col{12 − (−2);9 − 4} = col{14;5}
b) 3**p** = col{−3;6}. **r** − 3**p** = col{−2 + 3;5 − 6} = col{1;−1}
c) col{4 + 1 − 4;3 − 2 + 10} = col{1;11}
## ✏️ Example 11.3
Find the magnitude of the resultant q + r in Example 11.2.
**Solution**
**q** + **r** = col{2;8}. |**q** + **r**| = sqrt{2^{2} + 8^{2}} = sqrt{68} ≈ **8.25 units**

pages.title: Keep going
pages.body: > ✨ **Did you know?** Multiplying a vector by a positive scalar changes its length but not its direction. Multiplying by a negative scalar reverses its direction: −**q** = col{−4;−3} points exactly opposite to **q**.

pages.title: Exercise 11.1
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 11.1** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. Given **a** = col{2;−3}, **b** = col{−1;4} and **c** = col{5;0}, find: a) **a** + **b** b) **b** − **c** c) 2**a** + 3**b** d) **a** − **b** + **c** e) 4**c** − 2**a**
2. Find the magnitude of: a) **a** + **b** b) 2**a** + 3**b**
3. On squared paper draw **a**, **b** and **a** + **b** nose to tail.
4. A boat sails col{6;2} km and then col{−2;5} km. Find its total displacement and its distance from the start.

On squared paper draw **a**, **b** and **a** + **b** nose to tail.

pages.title: Equal vectors
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Demonstrate understanding of vector equality.
Curriculum indicator B8.3.2.2.2
> 🔑 **Key idea: Equal vectors** — Two vectors are **equal** if they have the **same magnitude and the same direction**. In component form, col{a;b} = col{c;d} if and only if **a = c and b = d**. Equal vectors may start at different points.
[[fig:m8-f44|Figure 11.2: The three arrows represent the same (equal) vector]]
## ✏️ Example 11.4
If a = col{3;5}, b = col{7;2} and c = col{−3;4}, calculate |p| where p = a + [[1/2]](b − c).
**Solution**
**b** − **c** = col{10;−2}; [[1/2]](**b** − **c**) = col{5;−1}; **p** = col{3 + 5;5 − 1} = col{8;4}
|**p**| = sqrt{64 + 16} = sqrt{80} ≈ **8.94**
## ✏️ Example 11.5
If M = N, find x and y given that M = col{x − 2;x − y} and N = col{1;2x − 1}.
**Solution**
Equate components:
x − 2 = 1 ⟹ **x = 3**
x − y = 2x − 1 ⟹ 3 − y = 5 ⟹ **y = −2**

pages.title: Exercise 11.2
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 11.2** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. Find x and y if col{2x;y + 3} = col{8;−1}.
2. Find p and q if col{p + q;p − q} = col{10;4}.
3. ABCD is a parallelogram with A(1, 2), B(5, 3) and C(7, 7). Use vec{AB} = vec{DC} to find D.
4. If **u** = col{2;1} and **v** = col{k;3} and 2**u** + **v** = col{1;5}, find k.

questions.q: Find x and y if col{2x;y + 3} = col{8;−1}.
Find p and q if col{p + q;p − q} = col{10;4}.
ABCD is a parallelogram with A(1, 2), B(5, 3) and C(7, 7). Use vec{AB} = vec{DC} to find D.

parts.a: vec{AB} = col{4;1}, so D = C − col{4;1} = (3, 6)

questions.q: If **u** = col{2;1} and **v** = col{k;3} and 2**u** + **v** = col{1;5}, find k.

pages.title: Chapter 11 summary
pages.body:
- Add vectors nose to tail, or add corresponding components.
- Subtract by subtracting components; kcol{x;y} = col{kx;ky}.
- Equal vectors have equal components (same magnitude and direction).

questions.q: If **m** = col{−3;4} and **n** = col{5;−2}, find 2**m** + **n** and its magnitude.
Find the vector **x** such that **x** + col{3;−1} = col{−2;6}.
P(2, −1) and Q(6, 2) are two points. Find vec{PQ} and |vec{PQ}|.
If col{3a − b;a + b} = col{9;7}, find a and b.
